title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page continues §IV, 'Un épinglage canonique' (a canonical pinning). S is a base scheme. M is a rank-4 Azumaya algebra over S, i.e. a twisted form of M_2(O_S). It is equivalent data to a form G of GL(2)_S, SG of SL(2)_S or PG of PGL(2)_S, and to a P^1-bundle P over S, which parametrises the Borel subgroups.

On the previous page, a Borel one-parameter additive subgroup of SG is obtained from a section N of M that is nonzero on every fibre and satisfies Tr N = 0 and det N = 0 (equivalently N^2 = 0). The subgroup is the image of G_a under λ ↦ exp(λN) = 1 + λN.

This page makes three steps.

(i) Homothety. If N' = aN with a a unit (Grothendieck corrects a ∈ Γ(O_S) to a ∈ Γ(O_S^*)), then N and N' give the same subgroup.
- So these subgroups correspond to sections of the projective bundle of lines P̌(M), of relative dimension 3.
- Imposing Tr N = 0 cuts this down to sections of P̌(fM), a P^2-bundle, where fM is the trace-zero part (the form of sl_2).
- Imposing det N = 0 then gives the sections of the conic bundle {det = 0} in P̌(fM).
- In modern terms: the projectivised nilpotent cone of the twisted sl_2 is a conic bundle. It is canonically isomorphic to P itself, the space of Borels (the Veronese conic).

(ii) Unipotent version. Set e = 1 + N. Then (Tr N = 0, det N = 0) is equivalent to (3): det e = 1, Tr e = 2. These are the regular unipotent elements of SG; the next page uses Steinberg's terminology. Homothety of N becomes the equivalence e ↦ e^λ = 1 + λ(e − 1).

(iii) Justification. For e = λ + N with λ scalar in a rank-2 algebra:
- Tr e = 2λ + Tr N and det e = λ^2 + λ Tr N + det N;
- conversely, Tr N = Tr e − 2λ and det N = λ^2 − λ Tr e + det e.

Purpose. The aim is to set up a canonical pinning (épinglage) of forms of PGL_2 / P^1-bundles: choosing a section x_∞ of P makes P \ x_∞ an affine-line bundle. This presumably serves the 'équation des lacets' / Galois–Teichmüller programme, which needs canonical normalisations of P^1 with marked points.
errors: The formula 'Tr e = 2 Tr λ + Tr N' (and 'Tr N = −2 Tr λ + Tr e') is a notational slip. For scalar λ it should read Tr e = 2λ + Tr N, i.e. Tr(λ·1) + Tr N. The determinant formulas are correct.

Minor gap: sections of P̌(fM) correspond to line subbundles of fM, which are locally but not necessarily globally generated by a section N. The dictionary with global N up to Γ(O_S^*) holds only locally, or up to a twist by a line bundle. Grothendieck implicitly passes between the two.

ideas.what: For a twisted form of sl_2, Borel one-parameter subgroups correspond to points of the conic det N = 0 in the projectivised trace-zero part. This conic is the P^1-bundle of Borels.
ideas.modern_name: Projectivised nilpotent cone of sl_2 (Veronese conic) = flag variety
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; in the scheme setting SGA 3 (Demazure–Grothendieck)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (Borel subgroups and the scheme of Borels for reductive group schemes); EGA for P(E) conventions

ideas.what: Regular unipotent sections e with det e = 1, Tr e = 2, in bijection with square-zero N = e − 1. Homothety classes correspond to Borel additive subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: Regular unipotent elements (Steinberg); Springer-type isomorphism unipotent variety ≅ nilpotent cone for SL_2

ideas.what: Trace/determinant change-of-variable formulas for e = λ + N in a rank-2 Azumaya algebra.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, careful set-up of the dictionary between P^1-bundles, forms of PGL_2 / Azumaya algebras, and regular unipotents, preparatory to a canonical pinning. All of it is standard (SGA 3, Steinberg). It is interesting only as context for the 'équation des lacets' manuscript.
transcription_corrections: In the first line the inserted correction reads 'en fait, -- avec a ∈ Γ(S, O_S^*)'. The asterisk denotes units, consistent with the transcription.
'Tr e = 2 Tr λ + Tr N' is what is written. It is presumably intended as 2λ, not a transcription error.
Line 2 'e = e_N = [crossed] e_N(1) = 1 + N': the crossed word is illegible, possibly 'exp N'.
